newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian copper use surges on strong sectoral demand.
newsitem.headline: Asian copper use surges on strong sectoral demand.

text.p: Robust sectoral demand in the construction, transport and energy sectors will boost Asian copper consumption over the next few years, the International Copper Association's regional director said on Tuesday.
Peter Charlton said at a meeting partly organised by the Copper Development Centre in Singapore that consumption has risen sharply and above the traditional two to three percent a year level.
"In Asia, copper growth has been two to three times higher than world consumption," he said, adding "there is no reason for it to slow down but in fact every reason for it to increase."

Charlton said one of the principal driving forces behind rising copper consumption is the massive infrastructure requirements of Asia, especialy in the use of building wire for industrial and residential areas.

"Some estimate building wire will increase at around 10 percent per annum for the next five years. I believe this is extremely conservative when you look at the potential demand in China, India and even Indonesia," he said.
Copper tubes will also be in great demand for potable water systems in Asia especially for the higher quality end of the market as the use of galvanised steel in the region recedes.
Governments around the region will also be tapping copper for use in eliminating their power problems.
"Copper is a natural partner in this process," Charlton said.
Copper consumption will also be strong in Asia's transport industry as rising affluence gives more people the means to buy cars. It will also increase in telecommunications and consumer goods.
